member.name: M:DotNetExtras.Common.Extensions.ObjectExtensions.GetPropertyValue(System.Object,System.String)
member.summary: Returns the value of the immediate or nested object property.
member.param: Name of the property (case-insensitive; can be compound with names separated by periods).
member.returns: Property value (or null, if property does not exists).

remarks.para: The code assumes that the property exists; if it does not, the code will return null.
The code handles both class properties and fields.

member.name: M:DotNetExtras.Common.Extensions.ObjectExtensions.IsEquivalentTo(System.Object,System.Object,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Checks if the source object is identical to the target (comparing all instance properties and fields).
member.param: If true, non-public properties and fields will be checked along with the public properties and fields.
member.returns: True if objects are equivalent, otherwise, false.

remarks.para: The source and target objects are considered equivalent if their data types are compatible (e.g. int and long are compatible) and they meet the following criteria:

item.para: For simple types, such as string, int, DateTime, etc., both the source and target values can be typecast to the same type and found equal.
For arrays, list, and collection types, both the source and target must contain the same number of elements, and each element of the source must be equivalent to the corresponding item of the target.

For dictionaries, both the source and target must contain the same number of elements, and each element of the source must be equivalent to the corresponding item of the target found under the same key.
For hash sets, both the source and target must contain the same number of elements, and the values in both hash sets must match.
Comparison of string values is case-sensitive.

member.name: M:DotNetExtras.Common.Extensions.ObjectExtensions.IsPartiallyEquivalentTo(System.Object,System.Object,System.Boolean)
member.param: Object we are comparing (if null, it is treated as a partially equivalent).
If true, non-public properties and fields will be checked along with the public properties and fields.
member.returns: True if the source objects is null, equivalent or a subset of the target; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: The source and target objects are considered partially equivalent if their data types are compatible (e.g. int and long are compatible) and they meet the following criteria:

item.para: For all data types, the nullvalue of the source object is considered a partial match of the target.
For simple types, such as string, int, DateTime, etc., both the source and target values can be typecast to the same type and found equal.

For arrays, list, and collection types, the source must contain the same or a lesser number of elements than the target, and each element of the source must be equivalent to the corresponding item of the target.
For dictionaries, the source must contain the same or a lesser number of elements, and each element of the source must be equivalent to the corresponding item of the target found under the same key.
For hash sets, the source must contain the same number or a lesser number of elements, and the values in both hash sets must match.
Comparison of string values is case-sensitive.

member.name: M:DotNetExtras.Common.NameOf.Skip(System.Object,System.Int32,System.Boolean,System.String)
member.summary: Returns a shortened name of the object, class, type, or property after removing the specified number of compound prefixes or suffixes.
member.param: Full or partial property name (can also be referenced using nameof).

Number of parts to be excluded from the result. A positive number indicates skipping from the left, a negative number indicates skipping from the right. If the skipped number is bigger than the number of parts, an empty string will be returned.
If true, parameter names will be converted to camelCase.

member.name: M:DotNetExtras.Common.NameOf.Keep(System.Object,System.Int32,System.Boolean,System.String)
member.summary: Returns a shortened name of the object, class, type, or property keeping the specified number of compound prefixes or suffixes.
member.param: Full or partial property name (can also be referenced using nameof).

Number of parts to be included in the result. A positive number indicates including from the left, a negative number indicates including from the right. If the kept number is bigger than the number of parts, an empty string will be returned.
If true, parameter names will be converted to camelCase.
